what: Every key on which A, B and the official outputs (items 1-8) or A and B (item 9, B1) do not agree, including every number that one source holds and another lacks. Keys are results.json paths joined by '/'; a top-k list is two keys, '<path>/names' and '<path>/shares'; an interval object is four keys, '<path>/value', '/ci_low', '/ci_high', '/n_finite'.
tolerance: values and interval bounds: 1e-9 absolute or relative; n_finite exact; lists, sets and top-k names exact; top-k shares within 1e-9 position by position

sources.official_derived: keys no official file holds, rebuilt from official numbers with compare_shap.py's rules (a second check only)

status_codes.missing_in_first: the first source of the pair lacks the key
status_codes.missing_in_second: the second source of the pair lacks the key
status_codes.null_vs_absent: one source has null, the other lacks the key (no number either side)
status_codes.pairs: AB = A vs B, AO = A vs official, BO = B vs official, AOd/BOd = against the official-derived value

groups.cause: compare_shap.py writes no treeroute top 3 and no treeroute own-history share in fire's main row
groups.diagnosis: PROTOCOL.md section 8, main-text row: 'treeroute's top 3 variables; the consensus top 3; the own-history share of treeroute [CI] and of the median rival [CI]'; the brief, item 7: 'Fire's main set is treeroute alone: W and the pair statistics are undefined there, and treeroute's top 3 and own-history share still have values.' compare_shap.py main_text_row() writes treeroute_top3 and own_history_share_treeroute only inside 'if tr and rivals:' (lines 361-386), so fire's AW4_main_row.json and AW4_table.md hold neither. A and B agree on both numbers. The full-sample top 3 and share are in importance.parquet and families.parquet and equal A's and B's (derived check); the interval of the share is in no official file. Finding for the owner.

groups.cause: compare_shap.py does not recompute the sign agreement on the draws: no interval (finite_replicates written as 0)
groups.diagnosis: PROTOCOL.md section 8 lists the sign agreement among the 'Pairwise statistics, every pair, both levels' and says 'The importances, every statistic and every number of the main-text row are recomputed per draw. Percentile 95% intervals, each with its number of finite replicates.'; section 10 asks S3.13 for 'pairs x statistics with intervals'. compare_shap.py (lines 227-235) evaluates the sign agreement on the full sample only and writes ci_low = ci_high = NaN and finite_replicates = 0 although no draw was evaluated. A and B recompute it on every draw (that draw's top-10 union and signed means, the determined set fixed by the bootstrap interval) and agree on every interval. The full-sample values and the sign counts agree (A = B = official). No reported value changes; an interval the protocol's words ask for is absent. Finding for the owner.

groups.cause: a family with no variable (coral own history, defo context and calendar): A null, B and compare_shap 0
groups.diagnosis: Spec C15 ('a family with no variable in a problem'). compare_shap.py gives an empty family a zero row sum and share 0 (lines 268-274), and coral's main-row own-history shares 0.00 [0.00, 0.00] with 2,000 finite replicates; B does the same; A writes null with its why. The reported numbers are compare_shap's (0). No B1 problem has an empty family.

groups.cause: feature-level family-share distance: A null, B the variable-level number, compare_shap none (variable level only)
groups.diagnosis: Spec C15 ('whether the feature-level pairs carry a family-share distance, and from which phi'). Families are sums of variable-level phi (section 8), so A writes no feature-level family TVD; B repeats the variable-level value (its X03); compare_shap.py computes tvd_family at the variable level only (lines 281-295), which is A's choice. The variable-level family TVD agrees (A = B = official).

groups.cause: B1 feature-level family-share distance: A null, B the variable-level number
groups.diagnosis: The same open choice for the B1 pair. Section 10: the B1 numbers 'make the main comparison's choice (compare_shap.py), as the independent re-computation establishes it'; compare_shap has no feature-level family TVD, so A's B1 choice is the one to report. B's extra value equals its own variable-level B1 family TVD, which agrees with A's.

groups.cause: counts carry no interval in the official outputs (n_nonzero, sign_n_determined, sign_n_agree)
groups.diagnosis: Spec C08 (section 10: 'or whether a count gets an interval'). A and B recompute the counts on every draw and give intervals (they agree); per_lead.json nonzero_players and pairs.parquet signs_compared are full-sample counts only. compare_shap's choice: no interval for a count. The values agree; compare_shap counts nonzero players over J (line 333), A and B over each model's own columns (C09), with equal counts everywhere. For B1, section 10 says the B1 numbers 'make the main comparison's choice (compare_shap.py)', so B1's counts should be reported without intervals (their values stand).

groups.cause: the main row's range (min and max over the rivals) has no interval in the official output
groups.diagnosis: Spec C22 ('what the range reports (its two ends), and whether its ends get intervals'). compare_shap.py (lines 379-380) reports the full-sample min and max; section 8's row reads 'the median of the top-20-union Spearman [CI] and the range'. A and B give each end an interval and agree. The values agree.

groups.cause: the official main row names no 'median rival'
groups.diagnosis: Spec C23. compare_shap.py takes the median of the rivals' own-history shares (numpy median, line 385) and names no rival; A and B name the rival whose full-sample share is that median when the count of rivals is odd (defo and pm25: rival_lgbm). The median's value and interval agree (A = B = official).

groups.cause: item 8: the official outputs hold only the rows and the top-10 shares (over all variables), full sample
groups.diagnosis: Spec C25 ('which numbers the variable-level importances are ... over which set of variables the shares are taken ... whether these numbers get intervals'). compare_shap.py (lines 302-315) reports per arcsine model the number of rows with pre > 0 and the top 10 [name, share] (per_lead.json nonzero_forecast_rows, the AW3 table), with shares over every variable-level player of the problem; A and B add I, S, intervals, counts, the ranking and the regions used, with shares over the level's J. The numbers the official outputs hold (rows, top-10 names and shares) equal A's and B's; the share denominators differ only by the structural zeros, which are 0 on those rows.

groups.cause: importance.parquet holds no interval for I, s and S (full-sample values only)
groups.diagnosis: A and B give every player's I, share and signed mean a percentile interval with its finite count, and agree on all of them. compare_shap.py recomputes the importances on every draw (lines 201-208) but writes only the full-sample mean_abs, share, signed_mean and sign_determined (lines 245-248). Section 8 says the importances are 'recomputed per draw' (they are) and that intervals are 'Percentile 95% intervals, each with its number of finite replicates'; it does not say that each importance is reported with an interval, and section 10 lists for S3.13 'pairs x statistics with intervals ... each model's top-10 with shares; family shares'. Not one of the spec's C entries (spec 2.2 item 6: 'The format does not decide which numbers get an interval'). compare_shap's choice: no interval. No reported number changes.

groups.cause: families.parquet holds no interval for the family shares
groups.diagnosis: As for the importances: families.parquet holds each family's full-sample mean_abs and share (compare_shap.py lines 264-275); only the own-history share of the main row and the family TVD are bootstrapped. A and B give every family share an interval and agree. compare_shap's choice: no interval. No reported number changes.

groups.cause: fire's W and mean pairwise Spearman: official NaN with 0 finite replicates, A and B null
groups.diagnosis: The main set of fire is treeroute alone. compare_shap evaluates W and the mean Spearman on every draw and finds none finite (value NaN, interval NaN, finite_replicates 0); A and B write them as undefined by definition (null, n_finite null). Same meaning, different notation.

groups.cause: importance.parquet also holds rows for the structural zeros (players outside J)
groups.diagnosis: A and B report players of J only (spec 2.4: 'players holds one entry per player of J'); compare_shap writes one row per player and model, J or not. These 898 rows (3,592 numbers) have no counterpart in A or B; every one is exactly 0 (mean |phi|, share and signed mean) with sign_determined false.

groups.cause: families.parquet mean_abs has no results.json key
groups.diagnosis: Each family's region-weighted mean |row sum| (the numerator of its share). A and B report the family shares, which agree with the official shares; the unnormalised value has no key in the spec.

groups.cause: lists and counts that no official file holds, derived from official numbers by compare_shap's rules
groups.diagnosis: Rankings over J, the top-20 and top-10 unions, the determined-in-both sets, both_in_main_set, sign_n_agree, W's m and n, the main row's rivals, consensus shares and consensus top-3 shares, the region order and the global-index list are not written by compare_shap.py. Rebuilt from the official files with compare_shap's own rules (mapping.md), every one equals A's and B's.

groups.cause: A and B list different columns read from the lead's test set (an I04 record, not a number)
groups.diagnosis: A also lists the context columns it read and B the column 'issue'; both read the same records (the rivals' export, lead_0\test) and their global-index lists equal each other and per_lead.json's family map.
